[![Check the skill](https://github.com/Digitanomics/saas-defaults/actions/workflows/check-skill.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Digitanomics/saas-defaults/actions/workflows/check-skill.yml) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Digitanomics/saas-defaults)](https://github.com/Digitanomics/saas-defaults/releases/latest) [![Licence: CC BY 4.0 + MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-CC_BY_4.0_%2B_MIT-blue)](#licence) [![Rules: 11,689](https://img.shields.io/badge/rules-11%2C689-blue)](skills/saas-defaults/README.md#status) A skill for Claude and other AI coding agents that build web apps, SaaS products, dashboards, admin panels and marketing sites. You ask for a feature: a sign-up page, a table, a checkout. The agent builds the feature **and** the details nobody remembers to ask for: the states, the error paths, the backend safeguards and the emails. **11,689 rule cards**, **106 feature recipes**, 3 stack profiles. The agent opens only the cards a task needs. | You ask for | What an agent often builds | What it builds with the skill | |---|---|---| | "Add a sign-up page" | Email, password, a button | A show/hide toggle that keeps the caret; a strength meter only where a new password is set; a Caps Lock warning; the right `autocomplete` values; a refusal of breached passwords; the verification email | | "Handle failed payments" | A webhook that marks the account unpaid | Different screens for a failed renewal and a failed first payment; a message for the decline reason; the real next retry date; full access during the grace period; one "update card and pay" screen; read-only, not locked out | | "Add a create form" | Fields and a Save button | One form for create and edit; a guard against double submits; a warning before you leave with unsaved changes; each error inside its field; an idempotency key, so a retry does not create two records | The table shows typical examples of what the rules ask for. It is not the output of one measured build. For one real sign-up page built with and without the skill, with what it cost, see [the before and after example](examples/sign-up-before-after/README.md). **First test: an early result, not proof.** In a test with rules fixed in advance (10 tasks, one run each, skill v1.3.0, checklists and judges by Claude models), builds that were asked to use the skill scored 0.88 against 0.75 for builds without it, on a 0 to 1 checklist score. That is 0.137 higher (90% interval 0.108 to 0.166). Such builds cost about 3.5 times as much. We, the makers of the skill, wrote the tasks and ran the test, and many checklist items repeat details that the skill's own rules name. No version after v1.3.0 has been measured yet. [Method, data and what the test does not show](benchmark/README.md). ## Quick start In a Claude Code session: ``` /plugin marketplace add Digitanomics/saas-defaults /plugin install saas-defaults@saas-defaults ``` Then ask for a feature, for example: Add a sign-up page. Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, claude.ai and other agents: see [Install](#install). No setup is needed. Without a project profile, the agent works out your stack from the code, tells you what it assumed, and offers to create the profile for you. ## What it costs The skill folder is just under 25 MB on disk, but an agent does not load it all. It reads the router, then the recipe of the feature and the cards that recipe names. - **Reading.** In the first test, the prompt listed the skill. When it also asked the agent to use the skill, a build read about 54,000 tokens of skill text. When it only listed the skill, a build read about 34,000 tokens. These numbers were counted from the session transcripts, with v1.3.0. - **Money.** The model cost of a build that was asked to use the skill was about 3.5 times that of a build without it (2.7 times when the skill was only listed). Those builds also wrote about 2.7 times as many lines of code (2.3 times when the skill was only listed). On a subscription plan you pay no price per build, but a build with the skill uses more of your usage. - **When you are not building a feature.** In tools that support skills, the agent keeps only the skill's name and description in view (about 1,000 characters) until a task needs the skill. The optional always-on snippet adds about 6.5 KB of text to every session. - **Disk.** One copy per machine is better than one copy per project. The skill also ships an experimental shorter reading path, build packs: `scripts/find.mjs --recipe --pass1` prints the core and risk cards of a recipe for the start of a build, and `--pass2` prints the rest. Counted from file size on 13 sample requests, a session reads 14% to 41% less skill text this way. No real build has used the packs yet, they do not yet print every card a build needs, and the router does not use them. ## Help test it We are looking for people who try the skill on one real task and tell us what is wrong with it. Criticism helps more than praise. 1. Install the skill (see [Install](#install)). Note how many minutes it took. 2. In a small Next.js app (a fresh one is fine), ask your agent for **one** of these: "Add a sign-up page." · "Add a create and edit form for projects." · "Add team invitations." 3. Optional: build the same feature once more without the skill, in a second copy of the app. 4. Fill in the [Beta feedback form](https://github.com/Digitanomics/saas-defaults/discussions/new?category=beta-feedback) in the [Discussions](https://github.com/Digitanomics/saas-defaults/discussions) of this repository. Only three fields are required. "Nothing found" is a valid answer. **Time and cost.** We have not measured yet how long the task takes. In the first test (v1.3.0), one build with the skill cost about $5 to $8 of model usage. On a subscription plan it uses a part of your plan's limit instead. **The form is public.** You need a GitHub account, and your report shows under your GitHub name. Please remove keys, file paths and company names from anything you paste. **What the skill collects:** nothing. The skill is Markdown and a few small Node scripts. They read files and print text. Three of them can also write files when you run them: check lists and an index inside the skill folder, or check lists in a folder you name. They use only Node's own modules. No network calls, no hooks. ## Known issues - The first test measured v1.3.0. No later version has been measured yet. - In that test, a build with the skill cost about 3.5 times as much as a build without it. The test is an early result, not proof: the same model built and judged, each task was built once, and the checklists repeat many of the skill's own rules. - The install steps are tested by scripts on Linux, macOS and Windows: they copy the skill to each folder named in [Install](#install) and run its scripts there. On 22 Nov 2026 the maker ran two routes by hand inside Claude Code (the desktop app), on the maker's own account, with version 1.4.2: the plugin and the folder copy. Both worked. The other tools are not tested inside the tool yet. - Code notes: Next.js with Supabase is built in. Next.js with Drizzle and a separate API are extra folders you copy in. - A full read by Claude models confirmed 105 defects in the cards (under 1%) and 66 in the code notes. Ten serious ones, all in the code notes, are fixed (four in 1.4.1, six in 1.4.3). The others are not fixed yet. This was AI checking AI, so the real number is probably higher. - The RLS helper functions in the Supabase notes (rule `DATA-TENANT-63`) do not check that a membership is active. If your app can deactivate members, add that check to the helper functions and test what a deactivated member can still see. A full fix is planned. - A shorter reading path (build packs, see [What it costs](#what-it-costs)) exists as an experiment. It is not switched on. ## How it works The rules are short **cards**. Each card has an ID (for example `CMP-PWD-04`), a level (MUST, SHOULD or MAY), the kinds of app it applies to, the rule, the reason, and a `Check:` line you can test. Tags keep the rules in scope: a personal to-do app does not get enterprise SSO. The agent reads your project profile, finds the recipe for the feature, and builds in two passes: the Core list first, then the rest. It runs your checks and a pattern detector, and ends with a report of what it checked, fixed, skipped and could not verify. - **What it does, how it works, status and limits:** [skills/saas-defaults/README.md](skills/saas-defaults/README.md) - **The full guide:** [skills/saas-defaults/HOW-TO-USE.md](skills/saas-defaults/HOW-TO-USE.md) - **Changes by rule ID:** [skills/saas-defaults/CHANGELOG.md](skills/saas-defaults/CHANGELOG.md) ## Install Pick the route for your tool. Every route installs the same folder, `skills/saas-defaults/`. ### Claude Code, as a plugin (recommended) In a Claude Code session: ``` /plugin marketplace add Digitanomics/saas-defaults /plugin install saas-defaults@saas-defaults ``` Or from your shell, without a session: ``` claude plugin marketplace add Digitanomics/saas-defaults claude plugin install saas-defaults@saas-defaults ``` The skill then shows as `/saas-defaults:saas-defaults`. To update later: `claude plugin update saas-defaults@saas-defaults`. ### Any tool, by copying the skill folder Get the repository, then copy `skills/saas-defaults` into the folder your tool reads: ``` git clone https://github.com/Digitanomics/saas-defaults.git ``` | Tool | For all your projects | For one project | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/saas-defaults` | `.claude/skills/saas-defaults` | | Cursor | `~/.cursor/skills/saas-defaults` | `.cursor/skills/saas-defaults` | | Codex | `~/.agents/skills/saas-defaults` | `.agents/skills/saas-defaults` | | Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/skills/saas-defaults` | `.gemini/skills/saas-defaults` | | Antigravity | `~/.gemini/config/skills/saas-defaults` | `.agents/skills/saas-defaults` | For example, for Claude Code and all your projects: ``` # macOS, Linux, Git Bash mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills cp -R saas-defaults/skills/saas-defaults ~/.claude/skills/ # Windows PowerShell New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $HOME/.claude/skills Copy-Item -Recurse saas-defaults/skills/saas-defaults $HOME/.claude/skills/ ``` Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI also read `.agents/skills/` in a project, so one copy there serves all three. To update a copy: run `git pull` in the clone, delete the old copy and copy the folder again. ### Gemini CLI, as an extension ``` gemini extensions install https://github.com/Digitanomics/saas-defaults ``` The Gemini CLI documentation says that Antigravity CLI replaced Gemini CLI for some accounts on 18 June 2026. If that is your case, use the Antigravity step. ### Antigravity, as a plugin ``` agy plugin install https://github.com/Digitanomics/saas-defaults ``` ### Cursor and Codex, as a plugin The repository holds a plugin manifest for both (`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`). It is not listed in their plugin directories yet, so for now copy the skill folder as shown above. ### claude.ai Works on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra, and on Team and Enterprise when the owner allows skills. 1. Settings → Capabilities: turn on **Code execution and file creation** (skills need it). 2. Make a ZIP that holds one folder named `saas-defaults` with `SKILL.md` inside it: download or clone this repository and zip the folder `skills/saas-defaults` (about 8 MB zipped, just under 25 MB unpacked). 3. Customize → Skills → **+** → **Create skill** → **Upload a skill**, and choose the ZIP. 4. Turn the skill on. Current steps: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-using-skills-in-claude ### Other coding agents Put the folder in your project (for example `.agents/skills/saas-defaults/`). Then paste the block from `skills/saas-defaults/templates/AGENTS-snippet.md` into the project's `AGENTS.md`. If your agent does not know where skills live, add the folder's path to the pasted block. ### After the install The skill works without these steps: the agent works out your stack from the code and offers to create the project profile. Two optional steps make the agent use the skill every time: 1. **Project profile.** One short file about your app: stack, commands and product type. 2. **Always-on snippet.** A block for the project's `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` that sends every feature to the skill. The easiest way is to let the agent do it. Ask: "Create the saas-defaults project profile for this app. Fill in what you can from the code, and ask me about the rest." After the profile, the agent offers to paste the snippet. Both steps are explained in [skills/saas-defaults/README.md](skills/saas-defaults/README.md#make-sure-the-skill-is-used).
Optional, Claude Code only: a reminder at the start of each session The plugin ships no hook, so nothing runs unless you add it. If Claude Code often forgets the skill in your project, add this to the project's `.claude/settings.json` (or to `~/.claude/settings.json` for all projects). Claude Code then adds the one line to the context when a session starts. It costs a few tokens in every session, also in work that has nothing to do with features, so leave it out if the skill already loads well. ```json { "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "matcher": "startup", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "echo 'This project uses the saas-defaults skill. Load it before you build, extend or review a feature.'" } ] } ] } } ```
The check lists by rule ID are built from the cards, not stored here. To build them in your copy (Node 18 or newer, nothing to install): `node /scripts/build-checks.mjs`. **Folder size.** Keep the folder name `saas-defaults`: it must match the skill's name. The folder is just under 25 MB, so one copy per machine is better than one per project. **How the steps were tested.** The steps above follow each tool's own documentation, as we read it on 19 and 21 Nov 2026. An automated test copies the skill to every folder named above and runs its scripts from each copy (`.github/workflows/install-test.yml`). It does not start the tools. On 22 Nov 2026 the maker ran the plugin route and the folder copy by hand inside Claude Code (the desktop app), on the maker's own account (not a clean machine), with version 1.4.2. Both worked. The other tools are not tested inside the tool yet. If a step fails for you, please open an issue. **Stack profiles.** The skill folder holds the default stack profile, `next-supabase`. The other two, `next-drizzle` and `api-separate`, are in `extras/stacks/` of this repository, so the skill stays under the 25 MB limit of the skills installers. To use one, copy its folder into `stacks/` of your copy of the skill, for example `extras/stacks/next-drizzle` to `~/.claude/skills/saas-defaults/stacks/next-drizzle`. With a plugin install the tool manages the skill folder: copy the profile folder into your project instead, and write its path in your project profile. ## What is in this repository | Path | What | |---|---| | `skills/saas-defaults/` | The skill. `SKILL.md` is its entry point. This folder is all an agent needs | | `benchmark/` | The first test: its method, its limits and its data | | `examples/` | One sign-up page built with and without the skill: the page, the two diffs and the limits (its pictures are in `assets/before-after/`). An example, not a measurement | | `assets/` | The images of this page and of the benchmark page: the banner and the charts of the first test, each in light and dark | | `extras/stacks/` | The two other stack profiles, `next-drizzle` and `api-separate`. Copy one into `stacks/` of the skill when you need it (see Stack profiles above) | | `.claude-plugin/`, `.cursor-plugin/`, `.codex-plugin/`, `.antigravity-plugin/`, `gemini-extension.json` | One small manifest per tool, so the repository installs as a plugin or extension. Each one points to the same `skills/` folder | | `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-CODE`, `NOTICE.md` | The licences and third-party terms. The same three files are inside the skill folder | | `.github/` | This repository's own checks and templates | ## Licence Copyright (c) 2026 Digitanomics. | What | Licence | File | |---|---|---| | Rule text and documentation | CC BY 4.0 | [LICENSE](LICENSE) | | Scripts, check templates and code samples | MIT | [LICENSE-CODE](LICENSE-CODE) | Third-party licence terms and the check of the OWASP-based cards: [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). Thanks to the authors of the sources: [skills/saas-defaults/CREDITS.md](skills/saas-defaults/CREDITS.md). Not affiliated with Anthropic, OpenAI, Stripe, Supabase, Vercel or any tool named here. Names are used only to say what the skill works with. ## Contributing and security Found a missing detail or a wrong rule? See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Found a security problem in the scripts or in a rule? Please do not open a public issue; follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

The easiest way is to let the agent do it. Ask: "Create the saas-defaults project profile for this app. Fill in what you can from the code, and ask me about the rest." After the profile, the agent offers to paste the snippet. Both steps are explained in [skills/saas-defaults/README.md](skills/saas-defaults/README.md#make-sure-the-skill-is-used).
Optional, Claude Code only: a reminder at the start of each session The plugin ships no hook, so nothing runs unless you add it. If Claude Code often forgets the skill in your project, add this to the project's `.claude/settings.json` (or to `~/.claude/settings.json` for all projects). Claude Code then adds the one line to the context when a session starts. It costs a few tokens in every session, also in work that has nothing to do with features, so leave it out if the skill already loads well. ```json { "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "matcher": "startup", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "echo 'This project uses the saas-defaults skill. Load it before you build, extend or review a feature.'" } ] } ] } } ```
The check lists by rule ID are built from the cards, not stored here. To build them in your copy (Node 18 or newer, nothing to install): `node /scripts/build-checks.mjs`. **Folder size.** Keep the folder name `saas-defaults`: it must match the skill's name. The folder is just under 25 MB, so one copy per machine is better than one per project. **How the steps were tested.** The steps above follow each tool's own documentation, as we read it on 19 and 21 Nov 2026. An automated test copies the skill to every folder named above and runs its scripts from each copy (`.github/workflows/install-test.yml`). It does not start the tools. On 22 Nov 2026 the maker ran the plugin route and the folder copy by hand inside Claude Code (the desktop app), on the maker's own account (not a clean machine), with version 1.4.2. Both worked. The other tools are not tested inside the tool yet. If a step fails for you, please open an issue. **Stack profiles.** The skill folder holds the default stack profile, `next-supabase`. The other two, `next-drizzle` and `api-separate`, are in `extras/stacks/` of this repository, so the skill stays under the 25 MB limit of the skills installers. To use one, copy its folder into `stacks/` of your copy of the skill, for example `extras/stacks/next-drizzle` to `~/.claude/skills/saas-defaults/stacks/next-drizzle`.
